name: Upper South Ridge

pitch_detail.notes: Easier climbing regaining the ridgecrest after the first tower.
The route's 5th-class section - a downclimb off a large block, not an upward move.
A couple of ropelengths of Class 3-4 climbing, with a brief excursion to the ridge's left side around halfway up, to reach a false summit.
A couple more ropelengths from the false summit to the true (higher, north) summit.

descent_text: From the summit, follow the standard Class 3 route down to the west to the pass between Vesper and Sperry, then head south back over Headlee Pass and down to the car - do not try to reverse the South Ridge itself.
approach: Approach to Headlee Pass as for the standard route (see that route's approach). Cross the talus toward Vesper/Elan Lake, then take the first ramp heading up and to the right to reach the base of the South Ridge.
overview: A more technical, low-5th-class ridge scramble/climb on Sperry's south side - harder and more interesting than the standard route but without the commitment of the north/east face lines. It is heavily vegetated and not recommended for quality, though it is a real, documented line.
beta: Follows the standard approach to Headlee Pass, then crosses the talus toward Lake Elan/Vesper Lake and takes the first ramp up and right to the base of the South Ridge. The route climbs the ridgecrest with a brief detour onto its left side about halfway up: a ~200 ft, Class 4 first tower, then easier Class 2-3 climbing back to the ridgecrest, a 5th-class section (which is actually a downclimb off a block), then a couple more ropelengths of Class 3-4 to a false summit, and a couple more ropelengths beyond that to the true summit. Simul-climbing or moving unroped is recommended rather than pitching it out formally.
gear: Ice axe (for the Headlee Pass approach)
Crampons (optional, for the Headlee Pass approach)
